# Overview



CPPTRAJ is a fast, parallelized program designed for processing and analyzing molecular dynamics trajectory data and relevant datasets derived from their analysis. As a powerful computational chemistry tool, CPPTRAJ provides comprehensive capabilities for analyzing MD simulations from multiple popular software packages including [Amber](http://ambermd.org/), [CHARMM](https://www.charmm.org/charmm/), [Gromacs](http://www.gromacs.org/), and [NAMD](http://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/namd/). The program is distributed as part of the freely available AmberTools software package and also offers Python integration through [Pytraj](https://github.com/Amber-MD/pytraj) for script-based workflows.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L11-L20)

## Project Architecture

![CPPTRAJ Repository Structure](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj/blob/master/doc/gist.png?raw=true)

The repository follows a well-organized structure that separates source code, documentation, tests, and development tools. The architectural design emphasizes modularity, extensive testing, and support for multiple parallelization strategies.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L253), [doc/README.md](doc/README.md#L1-L9)

## Core Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    A[CPPTRAJ Core] --> B[Command Line Interface]
    A --> C[Parallelization Layer]
    A --> D[Analysis Modules]
    A --> E[Format Handlers]
    
    C --> C1[OpenMP]
    C --> C2[MPI]
    C --> C3[CUDA]
    C --> C4[HIP]
    
    D --> D1[Structural Analysis]
    D --> D2[Statistical Analysis]
    D --> D3[Energy Analysis]
    D --> D4[Clustering]
    
    E --> E1[Amber Formats]
    E --> E2[CHARMM Formats]
    E --> E3[Gromacs Formats]
    E --> E4[NetCDF]
    
    F[External Libraries] --> B
    F --> D
    F --> E
    
    F --> F1[NetCDF]
    F --> F2[BLAS/LAPACK]
    F --> F3[FFTW]
    F --> F4[ARPACK]
```

This architecture demonstrates CPPTRAJ's modular design where the core engine interfaces with multiple parallelization backends, analysis modules, and trajectory format handlers. The system leverages external scientific libraries for optimized mathematical operations.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L53-L82), [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt#L1-L50)

## Project Structure Overview

The repository is organized into logical directories that support development, testing, and documentation:

| Directory | Purpose | Contents |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| `src/` | Core source code | Main program implementation |
| `doc/` | Documentation | PDF manuals, LyX source files, bibliography |
| `test/` | Integration tests | 150+ test directories covering all functionality |
| `unitTests/` | Unit tests | Focused tests for specific components |
| `examples/` | Usage examples | Practical demonstrations (e.g., NIST-mAb preparation) |
| `dat/` | Data files | Atom type tables, residue name mappings, parameter files |
| `cmake/` & `cmake-cpptraj/` | Build system | CMake configuration modules |
| `devtools/` | Development tools | Utilities for developers, CI configurations |

Sources: [test/README](test/README#L1-L42), [examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/README.md](examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/README.md#L1-L25)

## Key Features and Capabilities

CPPTRAJ provides a comprehensive suite of analysis capabilities for molecular dynamics simulations:

### Trajectory Processing
- **Multi-format Support**: Native support for Amber, CHARMM, Gromacs (XTC, TRR, TNG), and NAMD trajectory formats
- **Coordinate Transformations**: RMSD calculations, structural alignment, rotations, and translations
- **Periodic Boundary Conditions**: Advanced imaging and unwrapping capabilities

### Statistical Analysis
- **Basic Statistics**: RMSD, RMSF, distance, and angle measurements
- **Correlation Functions**: Auto-correlation and cross-correlation analysis
- **Principal Component Analysis**: Dimensionality reduction and mode analysis
- **Time-Series Analysis**: Time-correlation functions and spectral analysis

### Structural Analysis
- **Hydrogen Bond Analysis**: Comprehensive H-bond detection and characterization
- **Secondary Structure**: DSSP-based assignment and analysis
- **Clustering**: Multiple algorithms including K-means, DBSCAN, and hierarchical clustering
- **Contact Analysis**: Native contacts and contact map generation

### Energy and Thermodynamics
- **Energy Extraction**: Process energy data from trajectories
- **Free Energy Calculations**: Thermodynamic integration and MM/PBSA methods
- **Lipid Analysis**: Order parameters and lipid-specific metrics
- **GIST**: Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory for solvation analysis

### Advanced Features
- **Normal Mode Analysis**: Eigenmode calculations and analysis
- **Wavelet Analysis**: Time-frequency analysis of trajectories
- **Diffusion Coefficients**: Calculation of molecular diffusion properties
- **Ensemble Analysis**: Support for REMD, MREMD, and HREMD simulations
- **PME Calculations**: Particle Mesh Ewald electrostatic calculations

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L29-L54), [doc/CpptrajManual.pdf](doc/CpptrajManual.pdf)

## Parallelization and Performance

CPPTRAJ offers multiple parallelization strategies to handle large-scale trajectory analysis:

| Parallelization Type | Use Case | Configuration Flag |
|---------------------|----------|---------------------|
| OpenMP | Multi-core shared memory systems | `-openmp` |
| MPI | Distributed memory clusters | `-mpi` |
| CUDA | GPU acceleration (NVIDIA) | `-cuda` |
| HIP | GPU acceleration (AMD) | `-hip` |

The system supports hybrid parallelization, combining MPI with OpenMP for optimal performance on modern HPC architectures. When using both MPI and OpenMP, users must properly configure thread allocation to ensure processes × threads does not exceed physical cores.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L83-L105), [configure](configure#L11-L35)

## Build and Configuration

CPPTRAJ provides flexible build options through both traditional configure scripts and CMake:

### Required Dependencies
- **Core Libraries**: NetCDF, BLAS, LAPACK
- **Compression**: Gzip, Bzip2
- **Optional Libraries**: FFTW (for PME), CUDA/HIP (for GPU acceleration)

### Bundled Libraries
CPPTRAJ includes several libraries internally but can use external versions if preferred:
- ARPACK (sparse matrix diagonalization)
- helPME (Particle Mesh Ewald calculations)
- XDR (Gromacs XTC format support)
- TNG (Gromacs TNG format support)

### Build Systems
- **Configure Script**: Traditional Unix-style build system with extensive options
- **CMake**: Modern build system with cross-platform support

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L53-L82), [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt#L1-L50), [configure](configure#L1-L50)

## Testing Framework

CPPTRAJ maintains an extensive testing infrastructure to ensure reliability:

### Integration Tests (`test/`)
- 150+ test directories covering all major functionality
- Named with descriptive `Test_X` convention
- Support for parallel testing via `DO_PARALLEL` environment variable
- Memory testing through valgrind integration
- Individual test execution support

### Unit Tests (`unitTests/`)
- Focused testing of individual components
- Tests for ArgList, StringRoutines, Range, NameType, and GistEntropyUtils
- Automated execution through UnitMaster.sh

### Continuous Integration
- GitHub Actions workflow
- AppVeyor for Windows builds
- Jenkins build status monitoring
- CodeQL security analysis

Sources: [test/README](test/README#L1-L42), [README.md](README.md#L4-L10)

1. **[Quick Start](2-quick-start)** - Learn the basics of running CPPTRAJ
2. **[Installation and Configuration](3-installation-and-configuration)** - Set up CPPTRAJ on your system
3. **[Basic Command Line Usage](4-basic-command-line-usage)** - Master fundamental commands
4. **[Trajectory Formats Support](5-trajectory-formats-support-netcdf-xtc-trr-tng-dtr)** - Work with different file formats

Once comfortable with the basics, explore specific analysis capabilities through the **Deep Dive** sections, starting with core concepts like **[Atom Selection and Mask Expressions](6-atom-selection-and-mask-expressions)** and **[Trajectory Processing Pipeline](7-trajectory-processing-pipeline)**.

> [!TIP]
> For optimal performance on multi-core systems, enable OpenMP parallelization during configuration (`./configure -openmp gnu`) and consider using the MPI build for distributed memory clusters (`./configure -mpi gnu`)

> [!TIP]
> The test suite (`make test`) is an excellent learning resource - examining test inputs and outputs in the `/test` directory provides practical examples of nearly every CPPTRAJ feature

# Quick Start



This guide provides a fast-track introduction to CPPTRAJ, helping you quickly set up, understand the basic architecture, and run your first molecular dynamics trajectory analysis. CPPTRAJ is a fast, parallelized program for processing and analyzing molecular dynamics trajectory data, supporting popular MD packages including Amber, CHARMM, Gromacs, and NAMD.

## Understanding CPPTRAJ Architecture

CPPTRAJ operates on a pipeline concept where you define analysis operations through commands or input files, process trajectory data, and output results in various formats. The program can read multiple trajectory and topology formats, apply transformations, perform calculations, and generate diverse outputs including coordinate files, data files, and visualizations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CPPTRAJ Analysis Pipeline"
        A[Topology File<br/>.parm7, .psf, .top] --> D[Analysis Engine]
        B[Trajectory File<br/>.nc, .xtc, .trr, .pdb] --> D
        C[Input Commands<br/>Interactive or File] --> D
        D --> E[Transformations<br/>RMSD, Alignment, Imaging]
        D --> F[Analysis<br/>Distance, RMSF, Clustering]
        D --> G[Output Generation<br/>.dat, .netcdf, .pdb, .mol2]
    end
    
    H[Configuration Options<br/>-openmp, -mpi, -cuda] --> D
    
    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#e1f5ff
    style C fill:#fff4e1
    style D fill:#f0f0f0,stroke:#333,stroke-width:3px
    style E fill:#ffe1e1
    style F fill:#ffe1e1
    style G fill:#e1ffe1
    style H fill:#f0e1ff
```

![CPPTRAJ Data Flow](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj/blob/master/doc/gist.png?raw=true)

The core architecture demonstrates flexibility in input handling and comprehensive analysis capabilities. You can interact with CPPTRAJ through interactive command mode or batch processing using input files, making it suitable for both exploratory analysis and automated workflows.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L9-L20), [README.md](/README.md#L65-L70)

## Project Structure Overview

The repository is organized to separate core functionality from tests, documentation, and examples. Understanding this structure helps you navigate the codebase and find resources quickly.

```
cpptraj/
├── src/                    # Core source code
├── test/                   # Comprehensive test suite
├── examples/               # Example usage scripts
├── doc/                    # Documentation (PDF/LyX)
├── dat/                    # Essential data files
├── cmake/ & cmake-cpptraj/ # Build configuration
├── CMakeLists.txt          # CMake build script
├── configure               # Configuration script
└── Makefile               # Make targets for building and testing
```

The `dat/` directory contains crucial reference data including atom type conversion tables, bond type mappings, and Karplus parameters for J-coupling calculations [dat/README](/dat/README#L1-L7). The `examples/` directory provides real-world usage scenarios, such as the NIST monoclonal antibody glycoform parameterization example [examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh](/examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh).

The `test/` directory contains over 200 test cases covering most functionality, organized in `Test_X` directories where X describes what's being tested. This serves as both a validation suite and a comprehensive examples collection [test/README](/test/README#L1-L15).

## Installation Methods

CPPTRAJ offers multiple installation approaches depending on your system configuration and requirements. The `configure` script provides the most straightforward installation method with extensive customization options.

### Basic Installation

For most systems, the minimal configuration suffices:

```bash
./configure gnu
make install
```

This builds CPPTRAJ with standard GNU compilers and basic functionality. The configure script automatically determines compiler and linker flags, generating `config.h` used by the build system [configure](/configure#L1-L15).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L75-L80), [configure](/configure#L16-L25)

### Parallel Configuration Options

For improved performance on multi-core systems or clusters, several parallelization options are available:

| Option | Description | Use Case |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `-openmp` | Enable OpenMP threading | Multi-core workstations |
| `-mpi` | MPI parallelization | Distributed clusters |
| `-cuda` | CUDA GPU acceleration | NVIDIA GPU systems |
| `-hip` | HIP GPU acceleration | AMD GPU systems |

These can be combined (e.g., `./configure -openmp -mpi gnu`) for hybrid parallelization. Note that when using both MPI and OpenMP, you should properly set `OMP_NUM_THREADS` so that (processes × threads) doesn't exceed physical cores [README.md](/README.md#L92-L95).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L82-L100), [configure](/configure#L17-L24)

### Library Dependencies

CPPTRAJ supports optional libraries for enhanced functionality:

| Library | Purpose | Optional |
|---------|---------|----------|
| NetCDF | Trajectory I/O | No |
| BLAS/LAPACK | Linear algebra | No |
| FFTW | FFT calculations (PME) | No |
| Gzip/Bzip2 | Compression | No |
| ARPACK | Sparse matrix diagonalization | Yes (bundled) |
| helPME | PME calculations | Yes (bundled) |
| XDR | GROMACS XTC support | Yes (bundled) |
| TNG | GROMACS TNG support | Yes (bundled) |

CPPTRAJ can automatically download and build missing libraries using the `--buildlibs` option. For example, `./configure -fftw3 --buildlibs gnu` will install FFTW if unavailable [README.md](/README.md#L105-L108).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L55-L70)

### Advanced Configuration

For systems with specific library locations or custom requirements:

```bash
# Use NetCDF from custom location
./configure --with-netcdf=/opt/netcdf gnu

# Use AmberTools libraries
./configure -amberlib gnu

# Static linking
./configure -static gnu
```

For a complete list of options, run `./configure --full-help` which displays additional debugging, library, and platform-specific options [README.md](/README.md#L75-L80), [configure](/configure#L27-L40).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L110-L115), [configure](/configure#L27-L43)

## Verifying Installation

After successful installation, validate your build using the built-in test suite:

```bash
# Run basic tests
make check

# Run verbose tests with error output
make verbosecheck

# Run unit tests
make unittest
```

The `test/` directory contains comprehensive tests that verify most functionality. Tests can be run in parallel by setting `DO_PARALLEL`, e.g., `DO_PARALLEL="mpiexec -n 2" make test.all` [test/README](/test/README#L5-L10), [Makefile](/Makefile#L25-L33).

> [!TIP]
> Always run `make check` after installation to ensure your build is functional. The test suite not only validates functionality but also serves as a rich source of usage examples covering diverse analysis scenarios.

Sources: [test/README](/test/README#L1-L15), [Makefile](/Makefile#L25-L35)

## Your First Analysis

Let's create a simple analysis workflow demonstrating core CPPTRAJ concepts. We'll calculate RMSD and distance measurements from a trajectory.

### Basic Input File Example

Create a file named `analysis.in`:

```bash
# Load topology
parm ../tz2.parm7

# Calculate distance between atoms 1 and 2
distance d1 :1 :2 out distance.dat

# Calculate RMSD relative to first frame
rmsd r1 first out rmsd.dat

# Process trajectory
trajin ../tz2.nc

# Run analysis
run
```

Execute this with:

```bash
cpptraj -p ../tz2.parm7 -c analysis.in
```

This demonstrates the fundamental CPPTRAJ workflow: specify topology, define analyses, load trajectory, and execute. The `:1` and `:2` syntax represents atom selection masks, which you can explore in detail in [Atom Selection and Mask Expressions](6-atom-selection-and-mask-expressions).

Sources: [test/Test_General/RunTest.sh](/test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L31-L40)

### Interactive Mode Example

For exploratory analysis, use interactive mode:

```bash
cpptraj

# In interactive mode
> parm ../tz2.parm7
> trajin ../tz2.nc
> distance d1 :1 :22 out distance.dat
> rmsd r1 first out rmsd.dat
> run
> xmgrace distance.dat  # Optional visualization
> quit
```

Interactive mode provides immediate feedback and is ideal for testing analysis commands before scripting them. Use `help [<command>]` to get information about specific commands.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L65-L70), [test/Test_General/RunTest.sh](/test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L31-L47)

### Real-World Example: Antibody Glycoform Parameterization

The repository includes a practical example demonstrating the `prepareforleap` command for parameterizing glycoforms:

```bash
parm mAb8671_2021_0526.pdb
loadcrd mAb8671_2021_0526.pdb name MyCrd

# Mutate PCA to GLN
change crdset MyCrd atomname from :PCA@OE to OE1
change crdset MyCrd resname from :PCA to GLN

# Prepare for LEaP parameterization
prepareforleap \
  crdset MyCrd \
  name Prepared \
  pdbout Prepared.pdb \
  leapunitname Mol \
  out Prepared.leap.in runleap leap.ff.in \
  nowat noh

# Output in Mol2 format
crdout Prepared Prepared.mol2
```

This example shows coordinate manipulation, residue mutation, and output generation—all core CPPTRAJ capabilities [examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh](/examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh#L25-L40).

Sources: [examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh](/examples/prepareforleap/NIST-mAb/RunExample.sh#L1-L49)

## Common Analysis Patterns

Based on the test suite examples, here are frequently used analysis patterns:

| Analysis Type | Example Command | Use Case |
|--------------|----------------|----------|
| Distance | `distance d1 :1 :2 out dist.dat` | Interatomic distances |
| Angle | `angle a1 :2@CA :3@CA :4@CA out angle.dat` | Bond/structural angles |
| Dihedral | `dihedral dh1 :1@C :2@N :2@CA :2@C out phi.dat` | Torsion angles |
| RMSD | `rmsd r1 first out rmsd.dat` | Structural deviation |
| RMSF | `atomicfluct out rmsf.dat byres` | Atomic fluctuations |
| Alignment | `align :1-5@CA ref tz2.rst7` | Trajectory alignment |

These commands can be combined in a single input file to perform comprehensive analyses. The test suite in `test/Test_General/` provides working examples of these patterns [test/Test_General/RunTest.sh](/test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L31-L55).

Sources: [test/Test_General/RunTest.sh](/test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L31-L55)

# Installation and Configuration



This guide provides comprehensive instructions for installing and configuring CPPTRAJ, the fast and parallelized molecular dynamics trajectory analysis program. You'll learn about system requirements, build system options, configuration parameters, and verification steps to get CPPTRAJ running efficiently on your system.

## Overview of Installation Methods

CPPTRAJ offers multiple build approaches designed to accommodate different environments and user preferences. The primary installation method uses a **configure script** that automatically detects system capabilities and generates appropriate build configurations. For users preferring modern build systems, **CMake support** is also available, providing cross-platform compatibility and integration with IDE workflows.

![CPPTRAJ Build Architecture](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj/blob/master/doc/gist.png?raw=true)

The build system architecture follows a modular approach where the configure script determines compiler flags, library availability, and optimization settings before generating the necessary makefiles. This process ensures that CPPTRAJ is built with optimal settings for your specific hardware and software environment.

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L1-L50), [configure](/configure#L1-L50)

## System Requirements and Dependencies

### Required Libraries

CPPTRAJ relies on several external libraries for core functionality. The following table outlines these dependencies and their purposes:

| Library | Purpose | Installation Notes |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| NetCDF | Trajectory I/O for Amber formats | Can be auto-built if missing |
| BLAS | Basic linear algebra operations | Can be auto-built or use OpenBLAS/MKL |
| LAPACK | Advanced linear algebra routines | Required for matrix operations |
| Gzip | Compressed file support | Standard on most systems |
| Bzip2 | Alternative compression format | Standard on most systems |
| C++11 Compiler | Language standard requirement | Required for PME functionality |

### Optional Libraries

Enhanced functionality requires additional libraries that CPPTRAJ can either use from your system or download and build automatically:

| Library | Purpose | Build Flag |
|---------|---------|------------|
| Parallel NetCDF | Parallel NetCDF trajectory output | Enabled with `-mpi` |
| CUDA | GPU acceleration for specific commands | `-cuda` flag |
| HIP | AMD GPU acceleration | `-hip` flag |
| FFTW | Fast Fourier transforms (PME support) | `-fftw3` flag |
| ARPACK | Sparse matrix diagonalization | Bundled with CPPTRAJ |
| helPME | Particle mesh Ewald calculations | Bundled, C++11 required |
| XDR | GROMACS XTC trajectory reading | Bundled |
| TNG | GROMACS TNG trajectory reading | Bundled |
| OpenMM | Energy minimization interface | `--with-openmm=PATH` |

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L70-L100), [configure](/configure#L50-L150)

## Using the Configure Script

### Basic Configuration

The configure script provides a straightforward interface for configuring CPPTRAJ. For most Linux/Unix systems with GNU compilers, the basic command is sufficient:

```bash
./configure gnu
make install
```

This command detects available libraries and compiler settings, generating a `config.h` file that controls compilation options.

### Configuration Options

The configure script accepts numerous options to customize the build. View available options with:

```bash
./configure --help          # Basic options
./configure --full-help     # All available options
```

### Compiler Selection

Specify your compiler suite as the final argument:

| Compiler Suite | Command |
|----------------|---------|
| GNU | `./configure gnu` |
| Intel | `./configure intel` |
| PGI | `./configure pgi` |
| Clang | `./configure clang` |
| Cray | `./configure cray` |
| Intel OneAPI | `./configure oneapi` |

### Parallelization Options

Enable parallel execution based on your hardware:

| Option | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `-openmp` | Multi-threading via OpenMP | `./configure -openmp gnu` |
| `-mpi` | MPI parallelization for clusters | `./configure -mpi gnu` |
| `-intelmpi` | Use Intel MPI compilers | `./configure -intelmpi` |

**Note:** You can combine `-openmp` and `-mpi` for hybrid parallelization. Ensure `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is set appropriately (processes × threads ≤ physical cores).

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L100-L120), [configure](/configure#L1-L50)

### GPU Acceleration Options

CPPTRAJ supports GPU acceleration through CUDA and HIP frameworks:

| GPU Type | Option | Environment Variable |
|----------|--------|---------------------|
| NVIDIA | `-cuda` | `CUDA_HOME` (default: `/usr/local/cuda`) |
| AMD | `-hip` | `HIP_HOME` (default: `/opt/rocm`) |

For CUDA builds, specify the compute capability using `SHADER_MODEL`:

```bash
SHADER_MODEL=sm_75 ./configure -cuda gnu  # For RTX 2070/2080
SHADER_MODEL=sm_80 ./configure -cuda gnu  # For RTX 3090/A100
SHADER_MODEL=sm_86 ./configure -cuda gnu  # For RTX 3080/4090
```

**Sources:** [configure](/configure#L50-L100)

### Library Management Options

The configure script provides flexible library management:

#### Automatic Library Building

For systems missing required libraries, CPPTRAJ can download and build them automatically:

```bash
./configure -fftw3 --buildlibs gnu    # Build missing libraries including FFTW
./configure --buildlibs gnu           # Build all missing enabled libraries
./configure --nobuildlibs gnu         # Disable library build prompts
```

#### Library Location Specification

Point to pre-installed libraries using `--with-<LIB>=<DIR>`:

```bash
./configure --with-netcdf=/opt/netcdf gnu
./configure --with-blas=/usr/local/lib gnu
```

#### Library Disabling

Disable specific libraries with `-no<LIB>`:

```bash
./configure -noarpack gnu    # Disable ARPACK
./configure -nofftw3 gnu     # Disable FFTW
```

#### Linear Algebra Frameworks

Optimized linear algebra libraries can improve performance significantly:

| Framework | Option | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Intel MKL | `-mkl` | Requires `MKL_HOME` or `MKLROOT` |
| OpenBLAS | `-openblas` | May need `--with-blas` |
| macOS Accelerate | `-macAccelerate` | Native macOS framework |
| Cray LibSci | `-libsci` | For Cray systems |

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L100-L150), [configure](/configure#L50-L150)

### Installation Directory

By default, CPPTRAJ installs to the current directory. Specify a custom location:

```bash
./configure --prefix=/path/to/install gnu
```

## CMake Build System

For users preferring CMake or requiring integration with CMake-based projects, CPPTRAJ provides comprehensive CMake support.

### Basic CMake Build

```bash
mkdir build
cd build
cmake ..
make install
```

### CMake Options

CMake provides options similar to the configure script:

```bash
# Enable/disable features
cmake -DUSE_ARPACK=ON ..
cmake -DUSE_TNG=ON ..

# Configure parallelization
cmake -DOpenMP_CXX_FOUND=ON ..
cmake -DMPI_FOUND=ON ..

# Build parallel combinations
cmake -DBUILD_PARALLEL_COMBINATIONS=ON ..
```

### Advanced CMake Configuration

CMake automatically detects available compilers and libraries. Override defaults with:

```bash
cmake -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ \
      -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc \
      -DNetCDF_DIR=/path/to/netcdf \
      ..
```

**Sources:** [CMakeLists.txt](/CMakeLists.txt#L1-L100)

## Installation Process

The installation workflow involves configuration, compilation, installation, and verification. The following diagram illustrates this process:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start Installation] --> B{Choose Build System}
    B -->|Configure Script| C[Run ./configure]
    B -->|CMake| D[Run cmake]
    C --> E[Generate config.h]
    D --> F[Generate Makefiles]
    E --> G[Run make install]
    F --> G
    G --> H[Binary in bin/cpptraj]
    H --> I[Run make check]
    I --> J{Tests Pass?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Installation Complete]
    J -->|No| L[Troubleshoot Build]
    L --> C
```

### Step-by-Step Installation

#### 1. Download and Extract

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj.git
cd cpptraj
```

#### 2. Configure

Choose appropriate options based on your system:

```bash
# Basic installation
./configure gnu

# With OpenMP and FFTW
./configure -openmp -fftw3 gnu

# With MPI for clusters
./configure -mpi gnu

# Using Amber libraries
./configure -amberlib gnu

# With CUDA support
SHADER_MODEL=sm_75 ./configure -cuda gnu
```

#### 3. Build and Install

```bash
# Single-threaded build
make install

# Parallel build (recommended for multicore systems)
make -j 8 install
```

The binary will be placed in `$CPPTRAJHOME/bin/cpptraj`.

#### 4. Verify Installation

Run the test suite to verify functionality:

```bash
make check
```

For verbose output showing test errors:

```bash
make verbosecheck
```

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L130-L150), [Makefile](/Makefile#L1-L46)

## Advanced Configuration Options

### Debug and Optimization

Control compilation optimization and debugging:

| Option | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `-debug` | Enable compiler debugging info |
| `-noopt` | Disable compiler optimization |
| `-tune` | Enable host-specific optimizations |
| `-d` | Debug info with no optimization (same as `-debug -noopt`) |
| `-timer` | Enable additional timing information |
| `-debugon` | Add `-DDEBUG` for internal debugging |

### Linking Options

Control how libraries are linked:

| Option | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `-static` | Use static linking for all libraries |
| `-libstatic` | Static link only specified libraries |
| `-shared` | Configure for generating libcpptraj.so |

### Special Features

Enable experimental or specialized features:

| Option | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `-single-ensemble` | Support single ensemble trajectory I/O |
| `-pubfft` | Use pubfft instead of FFTW (disables PME) |
| `-windows` | Configure for MinGW on Windows |
| `-profile` | GNU compiler profiling |
| `-vtune` | Intel VTune profiling support |

**Sources:** [configure](/configure#L100-L150)

## Using Amber Libraries

If you have AmberTools installed, CPPTRAJ can leverage pre-compiled libraries:

```bash
export AMBERHOME=/path/to/amber
./configure -amberlib gnu
```

This uses the BLAS, ARPACK, LAPACK, and NetCDF libraries from your Amber installation, potentially saving compilation time.

**Sources:** [README.md](/README.md#L100-L120)

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

### Library Not Found Errors

If configure cannot find a library:

```bash
# Specify library location explicitly
./configure --with-netcdf=/custom/path/to/netcdf gnu

# Or disable the library
./configure -nonetcdf gnu
```

### Linking Errors

For static linking issues, try:

```bash
./configure -static gnu
# Or static link only specific libraries
./configure -libstatic gnu
```

### Compiler Not Found

Specify compiler explicitly:

```bash
CXX=g++ CC=gcc ./configure gnu
```

### Fortran Compiler Required

Some features (ARPACK, PubFFT) require Fortran. Ensure a Fortran compiler is available:

```bash
FC=gfortran ./configure gnu
```

### Permission Issues

If you cannot install to system directories:

```bash
./configure --prefix=$HOME/cpptraj gnu
```

## Installation Verification

After installation, verify CPPTRAJ is working correctly:

```bash
# Check version
$CPPTRAJHOME/bin/cpptraj --version

# Run help
$CPPTRAJHOME/bin/cpptraj --help

# Execute basic analysis
$CPPTRAJHOME/bin/cpptraj -p test.prm -c test.rst -i basic.in
```

# Basic Command Line Usage



This guide introduces the fundamental command line interface patterns for CPPTRAJ, a fast, parallelized molecular dynamics trajectory data analysis program. CPPTRAJ provides flexible execution modes supporting both interactive command-line usage and scripted input files, making it suitable for both quick analyses and complex workflow automation.

![CPPTRAJ Terminal](https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj/blob/master/doc/CpptrajManual.pdf?raw=true)

## Architecture Overview

CPPTRAJ follows a command-driven architecture where operations are processed sequentially through a central dispatch system. Understanding this execution flow helps you structure your analysis workflows effectively.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A[Command Line Execution] --> B{Input Source}
    B --> C[Input File<br/>-i flag]
    B --> D[Direct Arguments<br/>-p, -y, -x flags]
    C --> E[Command Parser]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Command Dispatcher]
    F --> G[Parameter Files<br/>parm command]
    F --> H[Trajectory Input<br/>trajin command]
    F --> I[Analysis Commands<br/>distance, rmsd, etc.]
    F --> J[Trajectory Output<br/>trajout command]
    I --> K[Data Processing]
    K --> L[Output Files]
    J --> L
```

## Basic Invocation Patterns

### Running CPPTRAJ with Input Files

The most common way to use CPPTRAJ is through input files containing sequences of commands. This approach provides reproducibility and enables complex analysis pipelines.

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L1-L89)

**Basic syntax:**
```bash
cpptraj -i <input_file>
```

The input file contains one command per line, with each command following the pattern: `command [arguments] output <file>`. A typical input file structure includes:

```bash
noprogress                    # Suppress progress display
parm <topology_file>         # Load topology
trajin <trajectory_file>      # Load input trajectory
reference <ref_file>         # Load reference structure (optional)
<analysis_commands>          # Perform analyses
trajout <output_file>        # Write output trajectory (optional)
```

### Direct Command Line Arguments

For quick analyses, CPPTRAJ accepts essential parameters directly from the command line without creating an input file. This mode is particularly useful for single operations or batch processing.

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_CmdLine/RunTest.sh#L1-L48)

**Available command-line flags:**

| Flag | Purpose | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| `-p` | Specify topology file | `-p tz2.parm7` |
| `-y` | Specify input trajectory | `-y tz2.nc` |
| `-ya` | Specify trajectory frame range | `-ya "2 13 3"` |
| `-x` | Specify output trajectory | `-x output.crd` |
| `-xa` | Specify output trajectory options | `-xa "title MyTitle"` |
| `-i` | Input file containing commands | `-i analysis.in` |

**Example using direct arguments:**
```bash
cpptraj -p tz2.parm7 -y tz2.nc -ya "2 13 3" -y tz2.nc -ya "98 last" -x output.crd -xa "title MyTitle"
```

This equivalent command demonstrates how file wildcards work with CPPTRAJ:

```bash
cpptraj tz2.p* cmd.in
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_CmdLine/RunTest.sh#L30-L42)

## Input File Structure and Commands

### Essential File Loading Commands

**Parameter/Topology Files**
The `parm` command loads molecular topology information required for atom selection and coordinate processing:

```bash
parm tz2.parm7              # Load Amber topology
parm tz2.pdb                # Load PDB as topology
parm tz2.ortho.parm7 [WAT]  # Load with label
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L32-L36), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L49-L52)

**Trajectory Input**
The `trajin` command specifies trajectory files to process, with optional parameters for topology binding and frame ranges:

```bash
trajin tz2.nc                          # Load entire trajectory
trajin tz2.crd 2 13 3                  # Frames 2-13, stride 3
trajin tz2.nc 98 last                  # Frames 98 to end
trajin tz2.ortho.nc parm tz2.ortho.parm7  # With specific topology
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L28-L29), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L43-L52), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_CmdLine/RunTest.sh#L19-L24)

**Reference Structures**
Reference structures provide reference coordinates for analyses like RMSD calculations:

```bash
reference tz2.rst7                      # Load reference
reference ../tz2.nc parm tz2.parm7 1 [first]  # From trajectory, first frame
reference DPDP.nc parm DPDP.parm7      # With specific topology
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L31), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L51-L54)

### Basic Analysis Commands

**Distance Measurements**
Calculate distances between atom selections or to fixed coordinates:

```bash
distance d1 :1 :2 out distance.dat              # Between atoms
distance d2 :1@CA :2@CA out distance.dat         # Specific atoms
distance ToRef @1 @1 out distance.dat reference # To reference
distance Point :1 point 0.0 0.0 0.0 out dist.dat # To coordinate
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L27-L30), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_Distance/RunTest.sh#L14-L19)

**Angle Measurements**
Measure angles between three atoms:

```bash
angle a1 :2@CA :3@CA :4@CA out a1.dat              # Basic angle
angle a2 :2@CA :3@CA :4@CA out a2.dat.gz           # Compressed output
angle a3 :2@CA :3@CA :4@CA out a3.dat.bz2         # Bzip2 compressed
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L33-L36)

**Dihedral Measurements**
Calculate torsion angles:

```bash
dihedral dh1 :1@C :2@N :2@CA :2@C out phi2.dat       # Single dihedral
dihedral phi3 :2@C :3@N :3@CA :3@C out PhiPsi.dat    # Multiple to same file
dihedral psi3 :3@N :3@CA :3@C :4@N out PhiPsi.dat    # Append to file
datafile PhiPsi.dat noxcol                          # Format option
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L41-L46), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L47-L48)

**RMSD Calculations**
Calculate root-mean-square deviations with various fitting options:

```bash
rmsd r1 ref tz2.rst7 out rmsd.dat                 # Basic RMSD
rmsd r1a refindex 0 out rmsda.dat                 # By reference index
rmsd r2 :1-4@C,CA,N ref tz2.rst7 :1-4@C,CA,N out r2.dat  # Atom selection
rmsd r3 :2-5@CA ref tz2.rst7 :2-5@CA out r3-nofit.dat nofit  # No fitting
rmsd r5 first out r5.dat :2-5@N,CA,C nomod        # No coordinate modification
rms Res2-11 first :2-11 out rmsd.dat              # With dataset name
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L37-L41), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L52-L58), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L24-L28), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L103-L108)

### Trajectory Output Commands

**Basic Output**
Write processed coordinates to various trajectory formats:

```bash
trajout test.crd                                  # Amber trajectory
trajout test.nc netcdf                            # NetCDF format
trajout Restart/test.rst7 restart                 # Restart format
trajout test1.crd title MyTitle                   # With title
outtraj tz2.norotate.crd parm [WAT]               # After RMSD nofit
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L30-L32), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_CmdLine/RunTest.sh#L25), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L54-L55), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L58)

> [!TIP]
> Output trajectory formats are specified either by file extension (`.nc` for NetCDF, `.crd` for Amber text) or explicitly with keywords like `netcdf` or `restart`. Choose formats based on your downstream analysis tools and file size requirements.

## Advanced Command Patterns

### Multi-Topology Analysis

CPPTRAJ can process trajectories from multiple topologies within a single session, useful for ensemble systems or comparative analyses:

```bash
parm tz2.parm7          # Primary topology
parm tz2.pdb            # Secondary topology
trajin tz2.nc           # Associated trajectory
trajin tz2.ortho.nc parm tz2.ortho.parm7  # Different topology
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L32-L43)

### Advanced RMSD Options

For sophisticated structural analyses, CPPTRAJ provides additional RMSD calculation modes:

```bash
# Mass-weighted RMSD with vector saving
rms Res2-11_mass first :2-11 out rmsd.mass.dat mass \
  savevectors combined vecsout vecs.dat

# RMSD to reference trajectory
rms Res2_11_traj reftraj ../tz2.truncoct.nc :2-11 out rmsd.reftraj.dat

# RMSD with rotation matrix output
rms ROT ref [first] out rms.dat @CA savematrices matricesout rmatrices.dat

# RMSD to previous frame
rms ToPrevious :2-12@CA previous out Previous.dat
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L25-L30), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L31-L33), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L57), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L95-L98)

### Imaging and Distance Calculations

For periodic systems, use imaging-aware distance calculations:

```bash
# With minimum image convention (default)
distance EndToEnd :1 :13 out ortho.dat

# Without imaging
distance To553_noImage ^1 :553 out ortho.553.dat noimage

# Non-orthogonal box support
parm tz2.truncoct.parm7
trajin tz2.truncoct.nc
distance To385 ^1 :385 out truncoct.385.dat
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_Distance/RunTest.sh#L29-L35), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_Distance/RunTest.sh#L40-L47)

## Workflow Execution Patterns

### Complete Analysis Pipeline Example

A typical CPPTRAJ session follows this logical sequence:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Load Topology<br/>parm] --> B[Load Trajectories<br/>trajin]
    B --> C[Load Reference<br/>reference]
    C --> D[Define Analyses<br/>distance/rmsd/angle]
    D --> E[Execute Analysis<br/>run]
    E --> F[Output Trajectory<br/>trajout]
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L27-L58)

### Practical Example Script

```bash
noprogress                      # Suppress progress output
parm tz2.parm7                 # Load topology
trajin tz2.nc                  # Load trajectory
reference tz2.rst7             # Load reference

# Perform analyses
distance d1 :1 :22 out distance.dat
rmsd r1 :2-12@CA ref tz2.rst7 out rmsd.dat
angle a1 :2@CA :3@CA :4@CA out angles.dat

# Output results
trajout aligned.crd            # Write aligned trajectory
run                            # Execute all commands
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L26-L44), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L20-L32)

### Error Handling and Testing

Always validate your analyses by comparing results with known reference data. CPPTRAJ's test suite demonstrates this practice:

```bash
# Run analysis
cpptraj -i analysis.in

# Compare with reference
DoTest reference.dat output.dat
```

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_CmdLine/RunTest.sh#L26-L29), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L64-L84)

> [!TIP]
> Use the `noprogress` command in scripts to produce cleaner output and improve performance for long-running analyses. For interactive sessions, omit it to monitor progress.

## Command Summary Table

| Category | Command | Purpose | Common Options |
|----------|---------|---------|----------------|
| **File I/O** | `parm` | Load topology file | `[label]` |
| | `trajin` | Load input trajectory | `[start stop stride] [parm]` |
| | `trajout` | Write output trajectory | `[format] [title]` |
| | `reference` | Load reference structure | `[parm] [frame]` |
| **Analysis** | `distance` | Calculate distances | `out <file> [noimage] [point x y z]` |
| | `angle` | Calculate angles | `out <file>` |
| | `dihedral` | Calculate torsion angles | `out <file>` |
| | `rmsd` | Calculate RMSD | `out <file> [mass] [nofit] [nomod] [savematrices]` |
| **Execution** | `run` | Execute queued commands | |
| | `noprogress` | Suppress progress display | |

Sources: [RunTest.sh](test/Test_General/RunTest.sh#L26-L58), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_RMSD/RunTest.sh#L20-L33), [RunTest.sh](test/Test_Distance/RunTest.sh#L14-L21)
